title.narrative: PSH Amplifying Drug & Substance Abuse linkages to SRHR in Zim
PSH Amplifying Drug & Substance Abuse linkages to SRHR in Zim

description.narrative: Detta projekt kommer innefatta utveckling och implementering av en särskild kampanj mot drog- och drogmissbruk med syfte att öka medvetenhet och kunskap om negativa effekter av missbruk på SRHR och GBV bland ungdomar och vuxna inom åldersgruppen 15-40 år. Insatsen syftar vidare till att stärka målgruppens motståndskraft samt att öka tillgång till tjänster inom SRHR.

This project will include the development and implementation of a special campaign against drugs and drug abuse with the aim of increasing awareness and knowledge of the negative effects of abuse on SRHR and GBV among young people and adults within the age group 15-40 years. The effort further aims to strengthen the target group's resilience and to increase access to services within SRHR and mental health.

The project vision is to trigger discussion around Drugs and Substance Abuse (DSA) and its harmful effects on SRHR outcomes at family, community, and national levels to inspire young people to shun the behavior. The project goal is to contribute to reduced DSA among vulnerable populations including young people, and key populations. By improving knowledge of the harmful effects of DSA on SRHR and GBV, the project will change attitudes towards DSA, and equip beneficiaries with the skills and efficacy to prevent the behavior. Through SBCC interventions, the project will reach 2,000, 000 individuals with traditional mass media, 1, 600,000 individuals with digital and social media, and 150,000 individuals with interpersonal communication at the community level.
The projects seeks to achieve the following objectives:
-Reduced demand for DSA among adolescents and young people.
-Increased social support and empathy to reduce DSA through community engagements.
-Increased access to SRHR products and services through media campaigns and community engagements.
Anticipated Outcomes:
-Increased access to accurate knowledge on the negative effects of DSA on SRHR, and GBV among adolescents and young people.
-Improved participation by community leaders, parents/guardians, and influencers in promoting social support and empathy to reduce DSA.
-Increased uptake of SRHR services among adolescents and young people.

sector.narrative: Control of harmful use of alcohol and drugs

description.narrative:
A multimedia campaign called 'The Strength is In You' based on the Baseline survey and HCD insights was developed. The campaign aims to inspire young people to avoid drug use by highlighting the experiences of former drug users. It emphasizes the importance of willpower and self-determination in drug prevention and the significance of social support from family and community.
The campaign is driven by 6 champions aged between 24 and 38 years, with lived drug and substance abuse experiences. Six audio testimonials were produced for radio placement, while two videos were created for digital media. Additionally, a set of digital materials featuring the six champions were developed to supplement the videos. To support the outdoor visibility of the campaign, 9 Billboards were produced and placed across Harare (4), Bulawayo (2), Mutare (1), Gweru (1), and Masvingo (1).
A campaign microsite was developed to complement the digital media assets, acting as a landing page that provides additional campaign information.
A community engagement toolkit was created to support the campaign's implementation at the community level. This toolkit comprises key messages and methods that help programmers communicate effectively with PWUID and their caregivers.
